text.p: These are the leading stories in the Serbian and Montenegrin press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- SERBIA -
POLITIKA

- The ruling Socialist Party of Serbia main board elected three new deputy chairmen and appoinited several new members of the board with the aim of improving efficiency. It called all parties who were for sovereignty, dignity and prosperity of the country to join forces with it.
- Yugoslav President Zoran Lilic organised a reception for April 27, Yugoslavia Day, which was attended by Presidents of Serbia and Montenegro Slobodan Milosevic and Momir Bulatovic.
- Kragujevac Zastava cars has dispatched the fourth shipment of 800 cars to Egypt bringing to 1,920 the total number of cars delivered to that country.
- Furniture factory Simpo of Vranje has increased production in March by 27.8 percent and its foreign currency revene by 42 percent on the same month last year.
- The Serbian government has agreed to partly relieve the textile and leather sector from payments of taxes on wages.
- Serbia earmarked 4.2 million dinars for financing projects aimed at helping reduce energy consumption.
- Serbian tobacco producers call for clamp down on cigarette smuggling.
- Yugoslav air controllers started guiding planes over Bosnian air corridors Thursday after five-year break.
- Montenegro airlines made its first flight to Belgrade Thursday.
- Institute for immunology Torlak has concluded deals worth $11.5 million for sale of vaccines with Indian firms.
- Delegations of Bosnian Serb Democratic Party (SDS) and Bosnian Croat Democratic Union (HDZ) agreed in Pale on correction of inter-entity boundary lines.
NASA BORBA

- According to a poll conducted by Mark Plan agency 21.6 percent of those polled would vote for opposition coalition Zajedno and 14.9 for the ruling Socialist Party of Serbia if parliamentary elections were held now. Slobodan Milosevic would be re-elected president with 17.5 percent saying they would vote for him.
- Novi Sad mayor Bozidar Svilar says he may leave the Serbian Renewal Movement (SPO) party because of in-party disputes.
- Italian fashion house Versace opens boutique in central Belgrade.
POLITIKA EKSPRES
- Central bank is keeping the dinar exchange rate firm even at the price of bank insolvency and high interest rates, commentary.
VECERNJE NOVOSTI
- Yugoslav government says there are no radioactivity risks in the nuclear sciences insitute of Vinca.
- MONTENEGRO -
POBJEDA
- Montenegrin Parliament Speaker Svetozar Marovic received university delegation which voiced concern over political conflict between President Momir Bulatovic and Prime Minister Milo Djukanovic.
- Building dams on river Moraca for new power plants is the Montenegrin government's priority. Montenergro uses only 30 percent of its water potential at present.
- The republic's minimum salary for April will be 320 dinars.
- Montenegrin workers staged a rally demanding new jobs, new investments and outstanding wages and said they would call for early elections if their demands are not met in three months.
MONITOR
- Only emergency measures to transform Montenegro into a democratic state can save it from Milosevic's revenge, commentary.
- Montenegrin people's party will return to regular state of affairs after its extraordinary congress on April 26, says party president Novak Kilibarda. -- Belgrade Newsroom +381 11 222 4254
